mainTopic: Is a לחי or a קורה a real wall for throwing into a מבוי, and how do we tell a מבוי from a חצר?
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: a ברייתא is limited to a case where remnants of the wall (גידודי) remain. רב יהודה then rules that throwing into an unmerged מבוי makes one liable if it has a לחי, but exempt if it has a קורה. רב ששת objects that food (a שיתוף) cannot change a domain, and a ברייתא says the עירוב makes no difference. So the גמרא rewords רב יהודה's ruling: it is about an alley open on both ends. This shows that רב יהודה, like רבה, holds a לחי is a wall and a קורה is only a sign. רבא holds both are only signs, and he answers two challenges from ברייתות. The גמרא then turns to shape: רב rules that an alley as long as it is wide is a חצר, which needs a פס of four טפחים, and רבי יוחנן confirms that courtyard boards must be four טפחים wide. רב נחמן's tradition, as the גמרא explains it, makes any space longer than it is wide, even by a tiny amount, a מבוי. The amud ends by returning to the משנה's disciple who spoke in the name of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The case is where wall remnants remain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier difficulty by explaining that the ברייתא speaks of a case where pieces of the wall remain standing on the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where it has remnants of the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. It answers a question on a ברייתא by saying the ברייתא is talking about a special case, where leftover pieces of the wall are still standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula הכא במאי עסקינן narrows the ברייתא to a specific situation, so it no longer causes a problem. Because some of the wall still stands (גידודי), the breach is not complete. The space keeps its status, and the earlier difficulty goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (a formula that limits a source to a specific case)
Remnants or stubs of a wall left standing after a breach

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא narrows down exactly which case it's talking about.

phrases.english: Where it has remnants of the wall.
phrases.notes: רבינו חננאל and the רי"ף explain that the wall wasn't knocked down completely; stubs are still standing on each side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised on the previous amud on the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe a fully breached wall, which would create a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a breach where wall remnants remain, so the space keeps its status.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a side post makes it liable, a cross beam exempts
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that in a מבוי without שיתוף, throwing into it from the public domain makes one liable if it has a לחי, but exempt if it has a קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: An alley whose residents did not merge through shared food: if it was fixed with a side post, one who throws into it is liable. If it was fixed with a cross beam, one who throws into it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה starts a new topic. He says whether a person is liable for throwing into an unmerged alley depends on how the alley's entrance was fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי works as a real wall (מחיצה), so it completes the alley as a true רשות היחיד, and throwing in from רשות הרבים makes one liable. A קורה only works as a marker (היכר), not a wall, so the alley is not a full private domain and the thrower is exempt. Notice that רב יהודה also mentions 'did not merge'. That detail is what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open onto
They merged: the residents made a שיתוף מבואות with shared food
A side post at the alley entrance
A cross beam over the alley entrance
One who throws (here, from the public domain into the alley)

steps.confusionAlert: Both a לחי and a קורה allow carrying inside the alley. רב יהודה's distinction is only about the Torah-level liability of someone who throws into it from outside.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
An alley in which they did not merge,
if he fixed it with a side post,
one who throws into it is liable,
phrases.notes: The לחי counts as a wall, so the alley is a full רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: if he fixed it with a cross beam,
one who throws into it is exempt.
phrases.notes: The קורה is only a marker, not a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion, unrelated to the answer in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an unmerged alley, a לחי makes it a רשות היחיד, so a thrower is liable. A קורה does not, so a thrower is exempt.

steps.title: רב ששת: shared food cannot change the type of domain
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת infers from רב יהודה's words that a שיתוף would make a thrower liable even with a קורה. He rejects that, because food cannot turn a place into a private or public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: The reason is that they did not merge. So if they did merge, even if it was fixed with a cross beam, he would also be liable?! Does this loaf make it a private domain or a public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב יהודה's wording. He asks why the shared food should matter at all, since bread cannot change what kind of space the alley is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת reads 'did not merge' as a real condition. That implies a שיתוף would make the thrower liable even with only a קורה. But domain status comes from physical walls, not from food placed for a שיתוף. So mentioning the שיתוף makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
The reason is X; this implies that without X... (an inference from wording)
A loaf of bread (the food used for the שיתוף)
Private domain
Public domain

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic principle: a שיתוף or עירוב is a rabbinic tool for permitting carrying. It does not create the Torah-level category of a domain.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected to it:
The reason is that they did not merge in it,
which implies that if they did merge in it,
even if it was fixed with a cross beam, he would also be liable?!
Does this loaf make it
phrases.notes: He's not really asking. Of course a loaf of food can't change what kind of area it is!

phrases.english: a private domain or a public domain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's ruling from step 2 based on its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's condition 'שלא נשתתפו בו' (that they did not merge)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies a שיתוף would change the law even with a קורה. But food has no power to change whether a place is a רשות היחיד or a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: liable whether or not they made an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying one who throws into shared courtyards or closed alleys is liable whether or not an עירוב was made. This seems to contradict רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: Courtyards of many people and alleys that are not open through, whether they made an עירוב or did not make an עירוב, one who throws into them is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to argue against רב יהודה. It says throwing into a closed alley or a shared courtyard always makes one liable, with or without an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא backs רב ששת's point: an עירוב makes no difference to liability. It also clashes with רב יהודה's exemption in the קורה case. The ברייתא treats a closed alley as a full רשות היחיד and the thrower as liable, even without any שיתוף.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
Courtyards shared by many residents
Open through on both ends
They made an עירוב (joined domains through shared food)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's distinction between a לחי and a קורה, and his mention of 'no שיתוף', now face two problems. רב ששת's logic says food cannot change domain status, and a ברייתא says one who throws into a closed alley is liable whether or not an עירוב was made.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Courtyards of many people
and alleys that are not open through,
phrases.notes: Closed on one end, so they have the walls of a private domain.

phrases.english: whether they made an eruv or did not make an eruv,
one who throws into them is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a source from a ברייתא supporting רב ששת's objection and challenging רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that throwing into an unmerged alley with a קורה is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says throwing into a closed alley is liable regardless of an עירוב. That conflicts with an exemption in an unmerged alley and shows the עירוב is irrelevant.

steps.title: A corrected version of רב יהודה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the earlier version of רב יהודה's statement. It replaces it with a version about an alley that is not fit for שיתוף, where a לחי makes a thrower liable and a קורה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רב יהודה said: an alley that is not fit for שיתוף, if it was made usable with a לחי, one who throws into it is liable. If it was made usable with a קורה, one who throws into it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the earlier version of רב יהודה ran into problems, the גמרא says his statement must really have been worded differently. It gives the corrected wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old version tied the outcome to whether a שיתוף was made, and that was attacked from two sides. The new version removes שיתוף from the picture. It speaks about an alley that is open on both ends, so it is not a normal closed alley. Now the only question is whether the fix used a לחי or a קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא corrects the wording of a teaching)
Fit for a שיתוף, meaning a normal closed alley
He made it usable, so that carrying inside is allowed
A side post at the entrance of an alley
A crossbeam placed over the entrance of an alley

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not fit for שיתוף' does NOT mean 'no שיתוף was made.' It describes the kind of alley: one open on both ends, which is not a regular closed alley.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rav Yehuda said:
An alley that is not fit for merging,
phrases.notes: An alley open on two opposite ends.

phrases.english: if he made it usable with a side post,
one who throws into it is liable,
if he made it usable with a crossbeam,
one who throws into it is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from the ברייתא in step 4 by rewording רב יהודה's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-version (correcting the wording of the original statement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling depended on whether a שיתוף was made.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה's ruling is about an alley open on both ends, and it depends only on whether a לחי or a קורה was used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an alley open on both ends, a לחי makes the thrower liable, while a קורה leaves him exempt.

steps.title: Inference: a side post is a wall, a crossbeam is a sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רב יהודה holds a לחי counts as a wall and a קורה is only a reminder sign. רבה holds the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds: a לחי works as a wall, and a קורה works as a sign. And רבה also said this: a לחי works as a wall, and a קורה works as a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב יהודה's corrected ruling. It then notes that רבה said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thrower is liable only if the alley is a true רשות היחיד. That requires real walls. Since a לחי makes the thrower liable, it must count as a real wall (מחיצה). Since a קורה does not, it must only be a sign (היכר) that reminds people they are in an alley.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently / this shows that
He holds
Because it counts as a wall
Because it serves as a reminder sign only

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the sugya: is a לחי a real wall or just a marker? The answer decides whether throwing into such an alley is a Torah-level violation.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
a side post works as a partition
and a crossbeam works as a marker.
And so too Rabba said:
a side post works as a partition
and a crossbeam works as a marker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the principle behind the corrected ruling in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב יהודה and רבה, a לחי is a real wall and a קורה is only a sign.

steps.title: רבא: both are only signs
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees. He holds that both a לחי and a קורה are only reminder signs, not walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: both this one and that one work as a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opposing view. רבא says neither a לחי nor a קורה counts as a real wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, a לחי cannot turn an alley into a true רשות היחיד. So throwing into an alley that relies on a לחי would not make one liable on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: But Rava said:
both this and that
work as a marker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the view of רב יהודה and רבה stated in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both a לחי and a קורה are only reminder signs, not walls.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from a ברייתא about the side post
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אבא brings a ברייתא. It says throwing into an alley that has a לחי makes one liable, and without a לחי one is exempt. That suggests a לחי is a real wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אבא challenged רבא: one who throws into an alley, if it has a לחי he is liable, and if it has no לחי he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אבא attacks רבא's view using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes liability depend on whether a לחי is there. Liability requires a true רשות היחיד, which requires walls. So the ברייתא seems to treat the לחי as a wall, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source (a משנה or ברייתא)
It has a side post

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Abba raised an objection to Rava:
One who throws into an alley,
if it has a side post, he is liable,
if it has no side post, he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's view from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a לחי is only a sign
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes liability depend on the לחי. Liability needs real walls, so the לחי must be a wall.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא: three walls versus two
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא is really about how many walls the alley already has. If it needs only a לחי, it already has three walls, so the thrower is liable. If it needs a לחי plus something else, it has only two walls, so he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if the alley needs only a לחי, one who throws into it is liable. If it needs a לחי and something else, one who throws into it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He shows that the ברייתא is not saying the לחי itself is a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alley that 'needs only a לחי' is closed on one end, so it already has three real walls and is a Torah-level רשות היחיד. That is why the thrower is liable, not because of the לחי. An alley that needs 'a לחי and something else' is open on both ends with only two walls, so it is not a רשות היחיד and the thrower is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)
It needs only a side post
Something else, an additional fix

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה and רבה say a לחי is a wall and a קורה is a sign. רבא says both are signs. Under רבא, liability depends on whether the alley already has three real walls, not on the לחי.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבא's reading, the phrases 'has a לחי' and 'has no לחי' are not about the לחי itself. They describe what kind of alley it is: closed on one end (three walls) or open on both ends (two walls).

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
if it requires only a side post,
one who throws into it is liable,
if it requires a side post and something else,
one who throws into it is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יעקב בר אבא's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא makes liability depend on the presence of the לחי itself, which would make the לחי a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא distinguishes between an alley that already has three walls and one with only two. The לחי is not what creates liability.

steps.title: A challenge to רבא from רבי יהודה's two-houses case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אבא challenges רבא again, this time from a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה allows a person with houses on both sides of רשות הרבים to put a לחי or קורה at each end and carry in between. This seems to treat the לחי as a real wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said: Someone who has two houses on two sides of the public domain may put a side post here and a side post there, or a beam here and a beam there, and then carry in the middle. The חכמים said to him: You cannot make an עירוב in the public domain this way!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אבא brings a second challenge against רבא, who said a לחי is only a reminder sign. He quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems to use a לחי as a real wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two houses give two walls along the sides of the street. At the open ends, רבי יהודה lets a לחי or קורה close things off, and then carrying is allowed. It looks like the לחי is doing the job of a real wall, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
Furthermore; even more than that
The public domain
Carries and moves things around
Make an עירוב, permitting carrying

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'אמרו לו' is still part of the ברייתא. The חכמים are arguing with רבי יהודה. It is not the גמרא's answer. The challenge to רבא comes only from רבי יהודה's own view.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One who has two houses
on two sides of the public domain
makes a side post here and a side post there,
phrases.notes: At each open end of the street between the houses.

phrases.english: or a beam here and a beam there,
and he may carry in the middle.
They (the Rabbis) said to him:
One cannot make an eruv for the public domain this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ, יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבא, after the first one (from רבי יעקב בר אבא) was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a לחי is only a reminder sign and not a wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה lets a לחי at each end turn a street into a place where carrying is allowed. That only makes sense if the לחי counts as a real wall.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds that two walls are enough by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה holds two walls make a private domain by Torah law. The houses already give two walls, so the לחי is only a reminder sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, רבי יהודה holds that two walls are enough by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says רבי יהודה's case does not prove that a לחי is a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the two house walls already make the street a private domain by Torah law. The לחי at each end is not needed as a wall. It is only a rabbinic reminder sign. So the case fits רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
He holds
Two walls
By Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's view still stands. A לחי is only a reminder sign. In רבי יהודה's case the two houses already supply the walls the Torah needs.

phrases.english: There, Rabbi Yehuda holds:
two walls suffice by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying reason: the source's ruling rests on another principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לחי at each end was acting as a real wall, so the street became private.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two house walls already make it private by Torah law. The לחי is only a reminder sign, which matches רבא.

steps.title: A square alley cannot be fixed with a minimal side post
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: an alley whose length equals its width cannot be permitted with a לחי of any small size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: An alley whose length is equal to its width is not permitted by a side post of minimal size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ruling of רב about an alley that is as long as it is wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal alley is longer than it is wide, and a tiny לחי of any width is enough for it. An alley shaped like a square is treated more like a courtyard. A courtyard needs bigger side boards (פסין), so the usual minimal לחי does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: An alley, opening onto the public domain
Its length is equal to its width
Becomes permitted for carrying
A side post of any minimal width

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the shape of the space decides which fix applies. An alley gets alley rules, and a square space gets courtyard rules.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
An alley whose length is equal to its width
is not permitted by a side post of minimal size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about the rules of side posts and beams for alleys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A square alley (length equals width) cannot be permitted with a minimal לחי. It needs courtyard-style fixes.

steps.title: A square alley cannot be fixed with a one-טפח beam
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי quotes רב: an alley whose length equals its width is also not permitted with a קורה one טפח wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: An alley whose length is equal to its width is not permitted by a beam one handbreadth wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of רב on the same square alley, this time about a קורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual one-טפח קורה also works only for a real alley. Since a square alley counts like a courtyard, a קורה does not help. Together, the two rulings say neither alley fix works for a square alley.

keyTerms.meaning: A cross beam one handbreadth wide

steps.whatToRemember: An alley as long as it is wide is treated like a courtyard. Neither a minimal לחי nor a one-טפח קורה permits it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
An alley whose length is equal to its width
is not permitted by a beam one handbreadth wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling from רב, applying the same idea to a קורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A square alley cannot be permitted with a one-טפח קורה.

steps.title: A square alley is really a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא praises רב's rulings and explains them. A square alley counts as a חצר, and a חצר needs a פס of four טפחים, not a לחי or קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: How exact are the teachings of the elders! Since the alley's length equals its width, it counts as a courtyard. A courtyard is not permitted with a side post or a cross beam. It is permitted only with an upright board four handbreadths wide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the reason behind the two rulings of רב from Steps 12–13, and praises how exact they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alley is permitted with a לחי or קורה only when it is shaped like a real מבוי, meaning long and narrow. Once its length equals its width, it is treated as a חצר. A חצר has a stricter rule: it needs a פס of four טפחים. That is why neither a small לחי nor a one-טפח קורה helps.

keyTerms.meaning: The teachings of the elders (here, the rulings of רב)
Exact, precisely aimed
Courtyard
An upright board four טפחים wide
A side post and a cross beam, the usual ways to permit carrying in an alley

steps.confusionAlert: רב was not saying the לחי is too small. The issue is the shape: a square alley is a חצר, and a חצר is not permitted with a לחי or a קורה at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key distinction in the sugya: a מבוי is permitted with a לחי or קורה, but a חצר requires פסים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
How precise are the teachings of the elders!
Since its length is equal to its width,
it is considered a courtyard,
and a courtyard is not permitted by a side post or a cross beam,
but only by an upright board of four handbreadths.
phrases.notes: A פס is an upright board standing next to the opening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כַּמָּה מְכַוְּונָן שְׁמַעְתָּא דְסָבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב's rulings in Steps 12–13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An alley whose length equals its width is legally a חצר, so it needs a פס of four טפחים rather than a לחי or a קורה.

steps.title: Why not treat the side post as a narrow board?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why the לחי cannot simply count as a very narrow פס, which would permit the square alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: If anything bothers me, this is what bothers me. Let this side post count as an upright board of tiny width, and the alley should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises his own difficulty with the explanation he just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא has just said that a חצר needs a פס of four טפחים, so his question cannot assume that every פס may be tiny. He seems to think that in some courtyard cases, such as a breached courtyard, a פס of minimal width is enough. If so, a לחי, which can also be tiny, should count like such a narrow פס, and the square alley should be permitted.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If something troubles me, this is what troubles me
An upright board of minimal, tiny width
And let it be permitted

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי:
phrases.english: If something is difficult for me, this is my difficulty:
let this side post be like an upright board of minimal width,
and let it be permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a square alley, being a חצר, cannot be permitted with a לחי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a minimal-width פס can sometimes permit a courtyard, then a לחי of minimal width should work just like that narrow פס, so the square alley should be permitted.

steps.title: Courtyard boards must be four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא forgot רבי יוחנן's rule: a חצר's פסים must be four טפחים wide, so a tiny לחי cannot serve as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the upright boards of a courtyard must be four handbreadths wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא's question by pointing to a rule he had forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question assumed that a פס can be tiny. רבי יוחנן rules that a חצר's פסים must be four טפחים wide. A small לחי is therefore nothing like a valid פס, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It escaped his attention; he forgot
The upright boards of a courtyard

phrases.english: This escaped his attention,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: what Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
the upright boards of a courtyard need
to be four handbreadths wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתְּמִיטְתֵּיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the questioner's assumption by citing an authoritative rule he overlooked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חצר's פס may be of any width, so a tiny לחי could serve as one.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חצר's פסים must be four טפחים wide, so a לחי cannot replace them.

steps.title: Defining an alley and a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites a tradition. A מבוי that is longer than it is wide, with houses and courtyards opening into it, is permitted with a לחי or קורה. A square חצר needs a פס of four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We have a tradition. Which alley is permitted with a side post or a cross beam? Any alley whose length is greater than its width and has houses and courtyards opening into it. Which courtyard is not permitted with a side post or a cross beam, but only with a board of four handbreadths? Any courtyard that is square.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן sums up the topic with a received tradition that sharply defines a מבוי and a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי has two features: it is longer than it is wide, and houses and courtyards open into it. Only such a מבוי is permitted with a לחי or קורה. A square space is a חצר and needs a פס of four טפחים, which matches רב's rulings and רבי זירא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a received tradition
An alley
Greater than its width
Square

steps.whatToRemember: Longer than wide, with houses and courtyards opening into it: that is a מבוי, permitted with a לחי or קורה. Square: that is a חצר, which needs a פס of four טפחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical definitions that decide which method of permitting carrying applies to a space.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: We have a tradition:
What is an alley that is permitted by a side post or cross beam?
Any whose length is greater than its width
and houses and courtyards open into it.
And what is a courtyard
that is not permitted by a side post or cross beam,
but only by an upright board of four handbreadths?
Any that is square.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the discussion with clear definitions that agree with רב's rulings
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A space longer than it is wide, with houses and courtyards opening into it, is a מבוי and is permitted with a לחי or קורה. A square space is a חצר and needs a פס of four טפחים.

steps.title: Does only a square shape count as a courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording 'square חצר' in רב נחמן's tradition. Does that mean a round courtyard would not need a four-טפח פס?
steps.simpleTranslation: Square, yes; round, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the tradition from the previous step. It said a 'square' חצר needs a פס, and the גמרא asks whether a round one would really be treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, the word 'מרובעת' (square) suggests that only a square shape makes an area a חצר. That makes no sense, because a round enclosed area is surely also a חצר. So the גמרא pushes us to find out what 'square' really means here.

keyTerms.meaning: square
round
yes

phrases.english: If it is square, yes [it is a courtyard],
phrases.notes: The גמרא is drawing this out from what רב נחמן taught.

phrases.english: but if it is round, no?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back: surely a round area is a courtyard too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the tradition quoted by רב נחמן in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'square' in the tradition about a חצר needing a four-טפח פס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A literal reading would exclude round courtyards, which is unreasonable, so the wording must mean something else.

steps.title: Square means not longer than wide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the tradition is about length versus width, not shape. Longer than wide makes it a מבוי; otherwise it is a חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if its length is greater than its width, it is a מבוי, and for a מבוי a לחי or a קורה is enough. If not, it is a חצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reinterpreting the word 'square.' It does not mean a square shape. It means any area whose length is not greater than its width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real dividing line is length compared to width. An area longer than it is wide is a מבוי and only needs a לחי or קורה. Any area that is not longer than wide, whether square or round, is a חצר and needs a פס of four טפחים. Step 20 asks how much longer it must be, and step 21 answers that question.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it is saying, introducing a reinterpretation
its length is greater than its width
is enough, suffices

steps.confusionAlert: 'Square' here is not about geometry. A round area is also treated as a חצר, because what matters is that it is not longer than it is wide.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic test for telling a מבוי apart from a חצר: compare the length to the width.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to explain that teaching in a new way.

phrases.english: If its length is greater than its width,
it is an alleyway,
and for an alleyway a side post or a cross beam is enough,
but if not, it is a courtyard.
phrases.notes: Includes square and round shapes alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording: 'square' means not longer than wide.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an area with a square shape is a חצר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any area not longer than wide is a חצר. An area longer than wide is a מבוי.

steps.title: How much longer must a מבוי be? שמואל's first view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much longer than wide an area must be to count as a מבוי. שמואל first thought its length must be double its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much [longer must it be]? שמואל thought to say: only once its length is double its width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the rule just stated. It then reports שמואל's first assumption, and this sets up the correction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know that 'longer than wide' makes a מבוי, we need to know how much longer counts. שמואל assumed a large margin: the length must be twice the width. The words 'סבר... למימר' hint that this was only his initial thought, which will be corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: and how much?
he thought to say, an initial assumption that gets revised
double, twice as much

phrases.english: And how much [longer]?
Shmuel thought to say:
Only once [its length] is double its width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measurement behind the 'longer than wide' rule set out in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much the length must exceed the width for the area to be a מבוי.

steps.title: Even slightly longer is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב tells שמואל that his uncle רבי חייא said even a tiny excess of length over width makes the area a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: my uncle said this: even a minimal amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב corrects שמואל's assumption by quoting a tradition from his uncle, רבי חייא. Any amount of extra length, however small, is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל required the length to be double the width, but רבי חייא's tradition removes any minimum. If the length is greater than the width by even a tiny amount, the area is a מבוי and a לחי or קורה is enough. This gives the final answer to the question 'וכמה'.

keyTerms.meaning: my uncle, referring to רבי חייא, רב's uncle
a minimal, tiny amount

steps.whatToRemember: An area longer than it is wide, even by a tiny amount, is a מבוי and only needs a לחי or קורה. An area not longer than wide is a חצר and needs a פס of four טפחים.

phrases.english: Rav said to him,
My uncle said this:
Even a minimal amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב, הָכִי אָמַר חֲבִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects שמואל's initial assumption in step 20 and answers the measurement question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any excess of length over width, even minimal, makes the area a מבוי.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה: the disciple who spoke for רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a תלמיד who spoke in the name of רבי ישמעאל, opening a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל, a certain disciple said, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the next clause. This sets up a new discussion of that disciple's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of length versus width is finished, so the גמרא moves on. It quotes the משנה's report of a תלמיד who spoke before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי ישמעאל. The 'כו׳' (etc.) means the rest of the משנה's words are understood, and the analysis will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: a certain disciple
in the name of
etc., the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael
a certain disciple said, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, where he said it in front of רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the length-versus-width discussion and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the משנה's report of a disciple's tradition in the name of רבי ישמעאל, for analysis.
